en: And I love gossip about the actors more than their work on-screen.
Yeah, you girls sure are into that sort of thing. Like tabloid shows and stuff.
I am frequently surprised when I see how foreign celebrities live their lives.
That's why I'm looking into getting my green card, so I can live in the US for a while.
It's a nice goal. The American Dream, right? When I played baseball, I dreamt of playing in the majors.
It's just all on a different scale than Japan. Knowing about the world makes a big difference in the way you see things.
You should definitely take a trip there, at least once.
What's so great about America?
For one, they're not pressed for time like we are in Japan. Everyone there values their personal lives over their work.
Plus, it's all so big and vast. I feel like there'd really be room to live, you know?
Gotcha. I wish I could live like that.
Green card?
That's what they call their proof of permanent residency. The ID card itself used to be green in color.
Permanent residency!? That's a big decision!
So, how do you go about getting one of these green cards?
I suppose the fastest way would be to marry an American man. My mother earned her Japanese residency by marrying my Japanese father.
Oh right, you're half-Japanese.
You can also enter a lottery for one, but they only hold it once a year, and only one in every few thousand people gets one.
Why not get married then? It sounds like the most expedient route.
Because choosing a spouse is not that simple. Up and marrying someone, without taking proper time to determine if he'll be a good match, is rather... short-sighted.
I hear you. When it comes to foreigners, their culture is totally different too.
Maybe just taking a trip would be better than a long term residency.
I suppose. But it would be ideal to have a home in both America and Japan, so I can go back and forth at my leisure!
Wow, aim a little higher there, why don't you?
C'mon, so what? Just get married to someone. If it doesn't work out, you can always get divorced.
That's a textbook sham marriage. I don't want the stigma of being a divorcee over that sort of thing.
Besides, if you're not married for at least two years, your residency is restricted. And if I get divorced without good cause, it's revoked.
I see. The law seems pretty tight about that kinda stuff.
It's because a lot of people have the same deceitful ideas you have, Shinada-san.
Haha, guilty as charged.
You've really looked into this. I'm a little surprised.
Of course I have. It's something that affects my life. I'm not saying all of this for no reason.
You've really planned for your future. I could stand to learn a lot from you.
That's absurd. If it's that unlikely, what's even the point!?
They limit applicants based on certain criteria, but the number is still that small, yes. Maybe I'd be better off giving up.
I think you should. Going on an overseas business trip is one thing, but I haven't heard of many people who want to live there.
I just don't like the sense of being tied down here in Japan. I wish people here would be more open to moving around, like people in the West.
Yeah, but most people here are no good with English. I don't think we could deal with living overseas.
Keep at it. Moving to another country is a huge deal. You can't expect it to be that easy.
You're absolutely right, Shinada-san! I'll look and see if there's some other way I can get in.
Haha! That's the spirit.
Is there no other way?
Hmm. Perhaps if I were to work there? That's how baseball players get in, right?
Oh yeah! You could get employed by a foreign company. I believe in you, Shion-chan!
No, I couldn't do that. I want to live in the US on my own terms. If I'm working, it'll be no different than living here in Japan.
Isn't that a bit unrealistic?
And that's it?
Well, I suppose there's also refugee status or asylum.
Those sound even less likely to work. Maybe the typical approach really is the best way?
Oh my, trying to live in another country certainly is difficult. I really respect my mother for what she must have gone through.
Whew. I feel a little tired now.
Are you all right? You're not feeling overworked, are you?
No, there isn't anything wrong with me.
Come on, now. We're only getting started here. Cheer up!
Yes, of course. My apologies.
The girl who was assisting me earlier was rather inattentive, and she wound up upsetting my customer.
Sheesh, I hope you chewed her out for it. Can't girls get fired for angering a customer, especially another hostess's client?
I did indeed. I took her aside and gave her a warning. And she said, "Put a lid on it, you cranky old bitch!"
So I struck her, without a second thought.
I'd have slapped her too. Even if she wants to nab your regular client, she has to be a team player. Now she's learned her lesson.
Indeed. Lately, younger girls don't have any respect when speaking to their seniors.
Well, this is a cabaret club. A higher-end club would never hire girls like that.
You can't do that. You should have gone to the manager and had them reprimand her instead.
I can't do that. That would backfire on me.
If I got the manager to do that for me this time, I would surely fall victim to accusations of favoritism in the future.
The manager knows this goes on as well, so I doubt they would give their backing to any one single person.
I get you. Handling you girls must be rough. I feel like I've learned a lot about team management.
She's jealous of you. She isn't doing a good job herself and so she took out her anger on you.
Perhaps so. It can be rather tiresome to listen to someone who isn't up to the task.
You're certainly confident. But I guess having that confidence shows your caliber as a hostess.
Yes, but what really concerns me is that this girl hasn't been the only one.
Oh? There have been others?
I might go so far as to say it's been nearly all of them.
All of them!?
Everyone seems to have it in for me, and attacks me at every opportunity. Do you think I'm that much of a disagreeable woman?
Yeah, I can kind of see why the other girls around here don't like you.
Oh. I see. Why is that?
Your politeness could rub people the wrong way. Your style of talking is really refined and polite, so it may sound insulting to them instead.
You should try to be more direct with people. It'll make it easier for them to relate to you.
You think so? Then I shall try to be more mindful from now on.
Thank you for your advice, Shinada-san!
Heh. Though, honestly, I have a hard time imagining you speaking casually, Shion-chan.
Of course not. You're worrying too much.
Are you sure? I really shouldn't fret over it? Please be honest with me here.
Don't worry about it. Forget about what the other girls say.
I see. You're telling me what you think I want to hear, aren't you, Shinada-san?
Whoa, hey, no I'm not! Why don't you believe me?
I despise being lied to more than anything else. I thought at least you would be honest with me.
Hmph. If that's how you feel, maybe you should try to fix things yourself before asking other people.
I... think that I am an obstinate, prideful, and unlikable woman.
Hm. And do you want to change that about yourself?
Not in the slightest.
Haha. That's the answer I was expecting! I guess you've got nothing to worry about then. Live your life the way you want to.
Yes, I shall behave as I please! The other girls at this club are my rivals, and nothing good will come from being friends with them.
You'd sure have an easy life if you could simply change yourself just because someone told you to.
I don't know. I only really know the part of you that you present to me as my hostess.
Based on what you know about me is fine, Shinada-san. Do I strike you as disagreeable?
The next time I travel abroad, there's someplace I'd really like to go.
Oh? Where's that?
Can you guess? It's a casino!
I see. Maybe Las Vegas? There aren't any casinos here in Japan.
I wouldn't have expected that. You don't strike me as the gambling type, Shion-chan.
Oh, I've never tried. That's why I want to go to a casino at least once in my lifetime.
Hmm. I guess once could be a good experience.
It must have been fifteen years ago since I got close. When I was younger, my family and I went overseas and the hotel we stayed at had a casino.
But since I was underage, I wasn't allowed to go in. My father went by himself while my mother looked after me.
My father looked like he'd had so much fun when he came back, that I've always thought about going myself, once I grew up.
I get you. Now that you can go all by yourself, you finally have the chance to achieve that childhood dream of yours.
Yes. Which is why I'm thinking of going.
Sounds nice. You've been waiting fifteen years for a chance, so you should go and have fun.
Unfortunately, it doesn't look like I'll be able to travel overseas anytime soon.
Oh, really? That's a shame.
You should go soon. You can get in just about anywhere when you're in your twenties. Why haven't you gone before now?
Well, there have been... a number of things.
Oh wow, really? Well, then you should be able to make the trip soon, right?
What games would you play?
All sorts, I'm sure. Perhaps slot machines?
Neat! I hear it's crazy when you win big on casino slots. Supposedly, you can win more than ten billion yen!
I think if I hit a jackpot that big, I might have a heart attack!
I'd probably spend a whole month thinking about what I'd spend it all on.
With ten billion yen there's hardly anything you couldn't buy! No need to worry on that account.
I guess you're right! Ten billion sure would be amazing!
Maybe you shouldn't. Slots are really all about luck.
You should pick a game like poker or blackjack, where your skill allows you to have at least some impact on the outcome.
Oh, but if I'm not very good at those, won't I have better odds just leaving it to luck?
I guess that's one way to look at it.
Besides, wouldn't it be exciting to watch all those spinning reels and such?
Hahaha. I guess if you're not worried about making money, you should play what you want.
Have you tried pachinko slots? You don't need to go all the way overseas for that.
Oh, I hadn't considered that. I've never played pachinko slots myself.
Really? You should try them at least once. I think you'll still be able to enjoy the experience of playing a casino slot game.
Okay! As soon as I get the chance!
Just don't get hooked on them...
Maybe you shouldn't. Gambling isn't the sort of thing that always winds up being fun.
I think you should keep the happy memories you have and not ruin them.
Oh, do you not gamble yourself, Shinada-san?
Well, yes. But I don't recommend it, Shion-chan.
Well! How selfish of you to enjoy something for yourself while discouraging me to do it!
I guess that's true. But trust me, you won't understand unless you've messed up really bad.
At its core, gambling is all about luck. Skill can improve your odds of winning, but too much of it is outside of your direct control.
I lived in a world where competition was for keeps. I don't like fighting battles that are dependent on lady luck.
When my life is on the line, I want to succeed on nothing but my own merits.
You've really thought this through! I suppose, given the large sums of money riding on a game, it's irresponsible to not be serious about it.
I only want you to know where I'm coming from. Spending a little on this sort of thing is fine, but be careful not to go too far.
Are you particular about your clothing and footwear, Shinada-san?
Particular?
Do you prefer any specific brands, for instance?
Sure. Well, when it comes to sports gear at least. I want to spend my money on clothes and shoes that improve my performance, you know?
So you pick the best that there is! Wonderful!
Well, I wouldn't go that far!
Not really. Buying brands is all about showing off to other people, you know? I pick what I want based on what's good for me.
But what's wrong with catching other people's attention a little? Who knows what they're saying behind your back, anyways?
Yeah, I'd rather not think about that.
I'm guessing you have your faves, Shion-chan?
Oh, yes. But I don't buy things for myself, so I'm not sure I can really say that they're <Italic>my</Italic> favorites.
